title: Wolves striker Tolu Arokodare set to give statement to police after facing online racist abuse
content:
Wolverhampton Wanderers striker Tolu Arokodare is set to give a statement to police over the online racist abuse which head coach Rob Edwards says has left the player “upset and angered”.

Arokodare was targeted with racist messages on social media after Wolves’ defeat at Crystal Palace on Sunday.

The club immediately condemned the abuse and published screenshots of the messages and Edwards says he and Arokodare’s team-mates and colleagues have provided ongoing support this week.

“It’s been a really difficult week for him,” said Edwards. “He was upset and angered by it, understandably so. We’ve supported him and I’ve had a few individual chats with him.

“We’ve spoken about it as a group as well to make sure that we get around him and support him, then he’s had overwhelming support from a lot of Wolves fans and other people reaching out, which is really good.

“The Premier League have been in touch, so there’s support there, but again we’re talking about something that we are having to talk about far too many times.

“I’ve been a head coach or a manager a number of times when my players have dealt with this, and the sad thing is that all of them have had it before.

“They say ‘I’m OK, I’ve had to deal with it before’ and I think that’s what’s really difficult. That’s tough to hear, but it’s a fact and the unfortunate thing is we’re going to be hearing about it again in the future.

“There could be someone this weekend. There probably will be, which is, so, so wrong.”

Edwards said Arokdare would provide a statement in the coming days but admitted that, with the abuse appearing to come from overseas, the onus is on social media companies to clamp down on it.

“I know a lot of the abuses come from accounts from maybe the other side of the world and it’s difficult then to maybe track these people down.

“Tolu will be giving a statement at some stage over the next few days but it becomes difficult to stop that.

“Without going into the social media companies and the ones that are actually giving them the platform and whether they can do more — I’m sure they can — we’ll be hearing a lot more about this.”

Edwards said he became aware of the abuse after Sunday’s game and first spoke to Arokodare about it on Monday morning.

“By then the player care staff and everyone were getting around him and things were being put into place in terms of support and making sure we’re helping.

“He was quiet on Monday. You could see that he was upset and he was down, but in terms of his training and the football this week he’s been able to sort of shift that mindset.

“In the last few days I think we’ve seen the usual Tolu, especially when we’ve been out on the pitch.

“I said to him that as a middle-aged man in my 40s, and a white man, I can’t begin to put myself in his position.

“It just really angers me and it saddens me. I apologised to him that he’s having to go through this.

“But I can’t understand how he’s feeling because I’ve never had that, I’ve never had to deal with anything like that, but we’ll help in any way that we can.”
